newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to lose 15.1 bln shekels in 1997 revenue.
newsitem.headline: Israel to lose 15.1 bln shekels in 1997 revenue.

text.p: The Israeli government will lose 15.1 billion shekels in revenue in 1997 as a result of tax benefits, the Treasury's revenue administration said on Tuesday.
This represents 13 percent of paid tax revenues.

The lost revenue includes 6.7 billion shekels in tax benefits to the capital markets. Of this amount, 3.1 billion shekels is from benefits for investors in provident funds; 800 million from benefits to investors in other types of long-term savings plans; 1.4 billion from tax exemptions on interest paid on savings accounts; and 1.4 billion from a tax exemption on stocks.

The government will lose 1.6 billion shekels from tax exemptions on social security allowances; 900 million because of tax benefits from the law for encouragement of capital investment; and 1.2 billion because of an exemption from value added tax on fruits and vegetables.

The revenue administration said that if these benefits were eliminated it would be possible to lower the marginal income tax rate from 50 percent to 40 percent and the corporate tax rate from 36 percent to 29 percent without losing state revenues.
